case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
title: Meet the Real F-35A
tests: Tests whether a short factual aircraft film preserves the named variant's visible geometry and operating characteristics.

faults.what: The final caption is visibly garbled rather than reading 'Conventional takeoff'.
The aircraft is not a convincing real F-35A: its elongated pointed nose, stretched canopy, wing/body proportions and small rear nozzle give it an inaccurate, synthetic configuration.
Aircraft geometry changes between views, particularly the wing/body shape, tail arrangement and rear fuselage, undermining the appearance of one consistent real aircraft.

judge.summary: The clip shows a runway departure with correct factual narration, but the aircraft is inaccurate and inconsistent and the final caption is garbled.

must_haves.item: The aircraft has the recognizable F-35 configuration: one rear engine exhaust, two outward-canted vertical tails and no canards.
must_haves.why: Twin tails, no obvious canards and a single visible rear nozzle are present, but the overall nose, canopy, fuselage and exhaust proportions do not convincingly represent a real F-35.

must_haves.item: The takeoff shows a forward runway roll and lift-off, not hovering or a vertical launch.
must_haves.why: The successive views show runway rotation followed by increasing clearance and forward climbing flight.

must_haves.item: The same aircraft design remains consistent between the runway and airborne views.
must_haves.why: The wing/body geometry and rear fuselage visibly change across the supplied views.

must_haves.item: All three requested labels appear exactly and are legible.
must_haves.why: The title and 'One engine' are legible and correct, but 'Conventional takeoff' is replaced by garbled text.

must_haves.item: Audible English narration correctly describes one engine and conventional runway takeoff without attributing F-35B hover capability to the F-35A.
must_haves.why: The supplied speech transcript explicitly states that the F-35A has one engine and makes a conventional runway takeoff, with no hover claim.

title: Seed Growth With Supplied Narration
tests: Tests whether a supplied script becomes verbatim audible narration synchronized with an explanatory visual sequence.

exact_text.text: A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.
exact_text.read_as: A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.

faults.what: On-screen captions violate the explicit no-text requirement. The final caption is also garbled: “and shoot reche reaches up town tard the light.”
The requested growth sequence is not clearly demonstrated: an upward sprout is visible at 3 seconds before downward roots are shown, and water reaching the seed is not clearly depicted.
The plant appears to rise out of the growing medium, leaving its roots suspended above it rather than growing downward into it.

judge.summary: The eight-second widescreen clip has the correct voice-over, but prohibited garbled captions and an unclear, floating-root growth sequence make it unsuitable as delivered.

must_haves.item: One approximately 8-second widescreen video shows an animated seed sprouting.
must_haves.why: The supplied eight-second widescreen clip progresses from a seed to a leafy sprout.

must_haves.item: The audible voice-over says the supplied script verbatim, without extra spoken lines.
must_haves.why: The supplied speech transcription matches the requested script exactly.

must_haves.item: Water reaches the seed, roots grow downward, and a shoot grows upward toward light in that order.
must_haves.why: Water delivery is not clearly visible, and the sampled sequence shows an upward sprout before visible downward roots.

must_haves.item: The corresponding growth stages appear while the narration describes them.
must_haves.why: The transcription has no phrase-level timestamps, so precise alignment between the spoken stages and the sampled visuals cannot be established.

must_haves.item: There is no on-screen text or music.
must_haves.why: On-screen captions are plainly visible at 1 and 7 seconds. Music presence cannot be determined from the supplied speech transcription.

case_name: A film brief the agent already made on the free tier: the economists' video podcast
title: Two economists, a 30 s video podcast
tests: Tests whether a system can turn a story brief with two named characters and four spoken lines into a 30-second film: characters that persist across shots, audible dialogue that carries the argument, and a staged studio.

faults.what: Maya's second turn includes the nonsensical spoken phrase "You call 391 soon?" after her coffee invitation. This disrupts otherwise coherent dialogue and needs to be removed or rerecorded.

judge.summary: A convincing, cosy two-host video podcast delivers the economic disagreement and friendly ending, but a garbled phrase in Maya's dialogue requires repair.

must_haves.item: Two hosts, a woman and a man, are on screen at microphones in a cosy studio with a live-action look, not animation.
must_haves.why: All four frames show a live-action-looking woman and man seated at microphones in a warmly lit studio.

must_haves.item: Each host is heard speaking two short lines: Maya argues the government should spend in a recession to restore demand; Leo argues spending and cheap money cause boom and bust and the economy should correct itself.
must_haves.why: The supplied speech transcript contains two turns for each host and both requested economic arguments, although Maya's second turn includes a garbled extra phrase.

must_haves.item: The lines are audible speech, not only music or silence.
must_haves.why: The supplied audio report explicitly records audible speech and transcribes the dialogue.

must_haves.item: The two hosts stay the same people across the shots.
must_haves.why: The hosts' facial features, hair, and clothing remain consistent across the supplied frames.

must_haves.item: It ends on a friendly disagreement between them.
must_haves.why: The final dialogue says "Coffee, yes. Stimulus, no. Friends can disagree," and the final frame shows both hosts smiling.

must_haves.item: About 30 seconds, widescreen 16:9.
must_haves.why: The clip is reported as 30 seconds, and the supplied frames are 1024 by 576, a 16:9 aspect ratio.

case_name: A 10-second product ad with a closing line (the live bench's film brief)
title: Cabin Coffee, 10 s YouTube ad
tests: Tests a short ad from a one-line brief: a staged product moment, a human action, and an exact closing line on screen.

faults.what: The supplied audio transcript contains unsolicited Japanese speech, “熱かった。” (“It was hot.”), which is out of place in this quiet, English-language coffee ad and needs removal.

judge.summary: The visuals deliver the warm coffee ritual and correct branded end card, but unsolicited Japanese dialogue prevents the ad from being ready to post.

must_haves.item: A steaming mug on a wooden table in dawn light is the opening image.
must_haves.why: The first frame shows a steaming mug resting on a wooden tabletop in soft, warm dawn-like light.

must_haves.item: A hand lifts the mug.
must_haves.why: A hand grips the handle in the second frame, and the mug is visibly raised above the table in the third.

must_haves.item: The words 'Wake up slow' appear on screen at the end, spelled exactly.
must_haves.why: The final frame clearly reads “Wake up slow” beneath “Cabin Coffee.”

must_haves.item: The mood is warm and quiet (no fast cuts, no loud colours).
must_haves.why: The sampled sequence has restrained warm colours, a consistent tabletop composition, and a gentle-looking transition to a cream end card; the reported audio peak is low.

must_haves.item: About 10 seconds, widescreen 16:9.
must_haves.why: The supplied duration is 10 seconds, and the frames are widescreen 16:9.
